title: Artifact and Cache Security knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Artifact and Cache Security?
options: Artifacts and caches can expose sensitive data or be poisoned by untrusted jobs; limit access, avoid secrets, and separate trusted and untrusted workflows.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
questions.answer_key: Artifacts and caches can expose sensitive data or be poisoned by untrusted jobs; limit access, avoid secrets, and separate trusted and untrusted workflows.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of artifact and cache security: Artifacts and caches can expose sensitive data or be poisoned by untrusted jobs; limit access, avoid secrets, and separate trusted and untrusted workflows. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: A team is working with “Avoiding sensitive information in artifacts”. Which practice best fits this topic?
options: Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
Use an artifact for a file produced by a run, choose exact upload/download paths, set retention intentionally, and verify the downloaded file is from the intended run/job.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
questions.answer_key: Use an artifact for a file produced by a run, choose exact upload/download paths, set retention intentionally, and verify the downloaded file is from the intended run/job.
questions.explanation: Avoiding sensitive information in artifacts: Use an artifact for a file produced by a run, choose exact upload/download paths, set retention intentionally, and verify the downloaded file is from the intended run/job. Apply the guidance to the actual event, runner, permissions, or artifact boundary and test the relevant case.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to artifact and cache security?
options: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: Artifacts and caches can expose sensitive data or be poisoned by untrusted jobs; limit access, avoid secrets, and separate trusted and untrusted workflows. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
